Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National IET-Ghana honours Adom News journalist Kodwo Mensah Aboroampa at 40th anniversary Source : Myjoyonline.com 19 November 2026 7:08pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Adom News journalist Kodwo Mensah Aboroampa (Amos Kwofie) of the Multimedia Group has been honoured by the Institution of Engineering and Technology, Ghana (IET-GH), in recognition of his outstanding contribution to journalism and the promotion of engineering excellence in the country.
The award was presented at the institution’s 40th anniversary celebration, held under the theme, “ Engineering Excellence for Sustainable National Development ”.
The honour recognises Mr Aboroampa’s consistent media advocacy, which the institution says has helped increase the visibility of IET-GH, promote the engineering profession and raise public awareness of critical infrastructure and national development issues.
In a citation presented to him, IET-GH praised his exceptional professionalism, dedication and invaluable service to the engineering fraternity.
The citation specifically acknowledged his role in using journalism to highlight issues affecting the engineering sector and bring important conversations on infrastructure and national development to public attention.
“In recognition of your outstanding contribution to journalism and dedicated promotion of engineering excellence in Ghana.
“Your consistent media advocacy has enhanced the visibility of IET-GH, promoted the engineering profession and raised public awareness of critical infrastructure and national development issues.
“The Institution of Engineering and Technology, Ghana (IET-GH), proudly honours you for your exceptional professionalism, dedication and invaluable service to the engineering fraternity.”
The citation was presented on November 20, 2026, by the President of IET-GH, Engr Wonder S. Davor, F.PE.
Mr Aboroampa was among several distinguished personalities honoured at the ceremony, including President John Mahama, the Ga Mantse, Minister for Works, Housing and Water Resources Ahmed Ibrahim, and the immediate past President of IET-GH, Engineer Henry Kwadwo Boateng.
The recognition adds to the journalist’s contribution to public-interest reporting, particularly in amplifying issues of national importance and promoting conversations that support Ghana’s development.
The 40th anniversary celebration brought together key stakeholders to reflect on the engineering profession’s contribution to national development and the need for stronger collaboration in building sustainable infrastructure.
IET-GH’s recognition of Mr Aboroampa also underscores the important role of the media in promoting professional excellence, accountability and public understanding of the engineering sector.
